title: Future Time
subtitle: Will, be going to, and more

levels.title: Will and going to
levels.full: Simple Future: Forms of Will and Be Going To

lesson.title: Learn: two ways to say the future

items.title: Two ways, same idea
lines: will and be going to both talk about the future.
Here they mean the same.

examples.text: It will snow tomorrow.
It is going to snow tomorrow.

items.title: will never changes
lines: will + simple verb. That's all.
No -s. No to.
chips: ❌ The weather will to turn cold.

items.text: The storm ___ after midnight.

items.title: be going to
lines: am / is / are + going to + simple verb.
In fast speech it sounds like “gonna”.
chips: he / she / it is going to
you / we / they are going to

examples.text: The roads are going to be icy.

items.text: Athena ___ going to go to the beach.

items.title: Not, questions, short forms
lines: will not = won't. Question: Will it…?

examples.text: The snow won't melt soon.
Will it be icy tomorrow?
I'm not going to go out.

items.text: ___ the storm going to be dangerous?
items.why: going to needs be: Is the storm going to…?

lines: will + simple verb: It will snow. (No -s, no to.)
am / is / are going to + simple verb: It is going to snow.

examples.text: It will snow tomorrow.
It is going to snow tomorrow.
The snow won't melt soon.

items.text: The weather ___ be hot tomorrow.
Athena ___ going to go to the beach.
She will ___ a relaxing day.
Sergio and Yanni ___ going to join her in the afternoon.

items.text: They are going ___ come home after sunset.
The weather ___ cold tonight.
It ___ warm up for several days.
How ___ here?
John is going to be a heart surgeon. He wants to work with young children.
items.why: It's his plan, not a guess.

items.text: He is going to be a fantastic doctor.
items.why: It's the speaker's opinion about the future.

items.text: He'll be kind and patient with the kids.
items.why: A guess about how he will be.

items.text: He is going to graduate from medical school in June.
items.why: It's on the calendar: a plan.

items.text: John's wife is going to specialize in senior care.
She will be fantastic. She is so caring.
I think they're going to have very busy lives.
The climate ___ going to get warmer.
items.why: The climate = it → is going to.

items.text: Cities near the ocean ___ have more flooding.
Smartphones and tablets ___ going to replace computers.
Electric cars ___ be more common than gas-powered cars.
I don't think so. We ___ going to have flying cars.
I don't think so. Computers ___ be the main teachers in classrooms.
I ___ learn to speak English fluently.
My country ___ going to win the World Cup.
items.why: My country = it → is going to.

items.say: You'll need to turn in all your assignments by tomorrow.
We're going to review for the final exam on Monday.
items.why: We're going to = We are going to.

items.say: There'll be 50 questions on the exam.
You'll have the whole hour to complete the test.
It's a long exam. Sorry, but nobody's going to finish early.
items.why: nobody's going to = nobody is going to.

items.say: It's going to be a lot of work. Study hard!
items.why: It's going to = It is going to.

items.say: The results'll be available in my office the next day.

talk.title: Life in 2050
talk.task: Make 5 predictions about life in 2050. Use will, won't and be going to.
talk.claudePrompt: You are my English speaking partner. I am practicing the simple future with will and be going to. Ask me for my predictions about life in 2050, one topic at a time (climate, cars, phones, schools, my country, my own life). I answer with will / won't / am, is, are going to. Check that I use will + simple verb (no -s, no to) and the right form of be with going to.

lesson.title: Learn: will or be going to?

items.title: A guess: both are OK
lines: Predicting the future? Use will or be going to.

examples.text: It will be cloudy tomorrow.
It is going to be cloudy tomorrow.

items.title: A plan from before: be going to
lines: You decided earlier. Now you tell someone.

examples.text: Why did you buy this paint?
I'm going to paint my bedroom tomorrow.

items.text: I bought the tickets last week. We ___ see the concert on Friday.

items.title: Decide right now: will
lines: An offer or a sudden decision? Use will.
You had no plan before.

examples.text: The phone's ringing.
I'll get it.

items.text: This box looks heavy. — Here. I ___ carry it.
items.why: An offer made right now → will.

items.title: won't = refuses
lines: A person (or a thing!) refuses to do it.

examples.text: She won't tell me her age.
The car won't start.

items.text: Something's wrong. The lights ___ turn on.
items.why: A thing that “refuses” to work → won't.

lines: A guess → will or be going to. A plan made before → be going to.
An offer or decision right now → will. Refusing → won't.

examples.text: I'm going to paint my bedroom tomorrow.
The phone's ringing. — I'll get it.
The car won't start.

items.text: I'M GOING TO PAINT the house next week.

items.text: This letter is in French. Can you help me? — Sure. I ___ it for you.
Do you want to go shopping with me? I ___ to the mall downtown.
items.why: I already planned it → be going to.

items.text: Alice's Restaurant. I ___ you there around six.

Why does he have an eraser in his hand? — He ___ the board.
items.why: He already planned it → be going to.

items.text: Why is that little boy crying? — I don't know. He ___ me.
What's wrong? — The door ___. I think the lock is broken.

missions.title: A plan or an offer to help?

items.text: What are you going to do this summer?
options: I'm going to work at a summer resort in the mountains.
I'll work at a summer resort in the mountains.
items.why: Talking about plans → be going to.

items.text: Can you help me out? I need to get this check in the mail by noon.
options: Sure. I'm going to drop it off on my way to work.
Sure. I'll drop it off on my way to work.

items.text: Tell me again. Why are you leaving work early?
options: I'm going to attend my cousin's funeral.

items.text: Darn, this flashlight doesn't work.
options: Here, give it to me. I'm going to fix it for you.
Here, give it to me. I'll fix it for you.

items.text: Here's the broom. What did you want it for?
options: I'm going to sweep the front steps.
items.why: The plan came before asking for the broom.

items.say: The Costa family are going to expand their restaurant next month.
items.why: It is already decided: a plan.

items.say: Their son says: Don't worry. I'll help in the kitchen!
I think the new restaurant will be very popular.

talk.title: A fiasco!
talk.task: You are leaving for a wedding in 5 minutes and something goes wrong. Fix it with “We'll…”.
talk.claudePrompt: You are my English speaking partner. Role-play: we are leaving for a wedding in five minutes and something goes wrong (for example: the car won't start, there is a stain on my shirt, we lost the gift). You start with 'Oh, no. What are we going to do?' and describe the problem. I must suggest solutions with 'I know. We'll ...' or 'I'll ...'. Then give me a new problem. Check that I use will for decisions made at the moment of speaking.

talk.title: My plans
talk.task: Tell Claude 3 things you have already planned for this week. Use be going to.
talk.claudePrompt: You are my English speaking partner. Ask me about my plans for this week and this weekend. I answer with be going to for plans I have already made. Sometimes ask me for help with a small thing (for example: 'I can't open this jar') so that I offer with 'I'll ...'. Check that I use be going to for prior plans and will for offers.

levels.title: When + present
levels.full: Expressing the Future in Time Clauses

items.title: The time clause stays present
lines: After when, before, after, as soon as, until, while:
use the simple present, not will.

examples.text: When Bob comes, we will see him.

items.title: Time clause starters
lines: These words start a time clause.

examples.text: Before she leaves, she is going to finish her work.
I'll wait here until they come.

items.tip: ❌ when Bob will come   ✅ when Bob comes

items.text: As soon as the taxi ___, we'll be able to leave for the airport.
items.why: After as soon as → simple present.

items.text: After I get home, I ___ dinner.

items.title: Either part can come first
lines: Time clause first? Add a comma.
chips: When he comes, we'll see him.
We'll see him when he comes.

items.title: while + -ing, after + have done
lines: while: something in progress → am / is / are + -ing.
after: have finished = finish.
chips: after I finish = after I have finished

examples.text: While I am traveling in Europe next year, I'm going to stay in youth hostels.

items.text: I will go to bed after I ___ my work.

lines: After when / before / after / as soon as / until / while → simple present.
The other part of the sentence takes will or be going to.

examples.text: When Bob comes, we will see him.
I'll wait here until they come.

items.text: After the rain ___, I am going to wash the car.
I'm going to vacuum the inside before I ___.
Are you going to help me before you ___ to your friend's?
My dad ___ the garage after he has lunch.
items.why: The main part → be going to.

items.text: My dad is going to clean the garage after he ___ lunch.
While he ___ the garage later, he is going to listen to podcasts.
While he is cleaning the garage later, he ___ to podcasts.
items.why: The main part → be going to.

items.text: The garage ___ great after he finishes tonight.
The garage will look great after he ___ tonight.
I ___ to an English language course while I am sleeping tonight.
items.why: The main part → be going to.

items.text: I am going to listen to an English course while I ___ tonight.
Bakir will be here soon. I ___ here until he comes.
items.why: The main part → be going to.

items.text: I am going to wait here until he ___.
As soon as the snow ___, I am going to walk to the store.
items.why: After as soon as → simple present.

items.text: As soon as the snow stops, I ___ to the store and buy some groceries.
items.why: The main part → be going to.

items.text: After Michelle ___ with a B.A. next year, she is going to enter graduate school.
After she graduates, she ___ graduate school and work on an M.A.
items.why: The main part → be going to.

items.text: Then she ___ on for her Ph.D. after she gets her master's degree.
items.why: The main part → be going to.

items.text: She is going to go on for her Ph.D. after she ___ her master's degree.
What are you going to do as soon as class ___ today?
items.why: After as soon as → simple present.

items.text: Before you ___ to bed tonight, what are you going to do?
What are you going to do after you ___ up tomorrow?
What are you going to do when you ___ free time this weekend?
After you ___ this course, what are you going to do?
They are going to come soon. I'll wait here until they ___.
I will go to bed after I ___ my work.
items.why: finish or have finished. Not will.

items.text: Linda is going to leave soon. Before she ___, she is going to finish her work.

missions.title: Tia's business trip: find the mistakes

items.text: Tia [need] to leave work early.
options: Tia needing to leave work early.
Tia needs to leave work early.
Tia will needs to leave work early.

items.text: She is going to prepare for her business trip when she [will get] home.
options: She is going to prepare for her business trip when she gets home.
She is going to prepare for her business trip when she is going to get home.
She is going to prepare for her business trip when she getting home.

items.text: After she [is packing] her suitcase, she [rehearse] her presentation.
options: After she will pack her suitcase, she is going to rehearse her presentation.
After she packs her suitcase, she rehearse her presentation.
After she packs her suitcase, she is going to rehearse her presentation.
items.why: after + present. Main part: is going to.

items.text: Her father is going to watch her presentation after he [is finishing] dinner.
options: Her father is going to watch her presentation after he finishes dinner.
Her father is going to watch her presentation after he will finish dinner.
Her father is going to watch her presentation after he finish dinner.

items.text: While he [watch], Tia is going to ask him for honest feedback.
options: While he will watch, Tia is going to ask him for honest feedback.
While he is watching, Tia is going to ask him for honest feedback.
While he watching, Tia is going to ask him for honest feedback.

items.text: After she [is practicing] several times, she will not feel so nervous.
options: After she will practice several times, she will not feel so nervous.
After she practice several times, she will not feel so nervous.
After she practices several times, she will not feel so nervous.

items.text: She will [pays] some bills and [sending] a few work emails before she [is going] to bed.
options: She will pay some bills and send a few work emails before she goes to bed.
She will pay some bills and sending a few work emails before she will go to bed.
She will pays some bills and send a few work emails before she goes to bed.

items.text: She is going to fall asleep quickly because she [is knowing] that she is very tired.
options: She is going to fall asleep quickly because she will knowing that she is very tired.
She is going to fall asleep quickly because she knows that she is very tired.
She is going to fall asleep quickly because she know that she is very tired.
items.why: know is a state verb → knows.

talk.title: What are you going to do when…?
talk.task: Claude interviews you about today and tomorrow. Answer with a time clause.
talk.claudePrompt: You are my English speaking partner. I am practicing future time clauses. Ask me questions one at a time, such as: What are you going to do as soon as you finish studying today? What are you going to do before you go to bed tonight? What are you going to do after you wake up tomorrow? What are you going to do when you have free time this weekend? I must answer with a full sentence that repeats the time clause (for example: After I wake up tomorrow, I'm going to ...). Check that I use the simple present in the time clause and never 'will' after when, before, after, as soon as, until.

levels.title: Present for the future
levels.full: Using the Present Progressive and the Simple Present to Express Future Time

items.title: A plan? Use -ing
lines: am / is / are + -ing can mean the future.
Only for planned things.

examples.text: She is seeing Dr. North next Tuesday.
Sam is leaving at noon tomorrow.

items.title: Look for a future time word
lines: The time word tells you it's the future.

examples.text: After lunch, I am meeting a friend of mine.

items.text: I'm meeting a friend at the airport later tonight. When?

items.title: Not for rain
lines: Rain is not a plan.
So no -ing for the future.
chips: ✅ It is going to rain tomorrow.

items.title: A timetable? Simple present
lines: Schedules and timetables use the simple present.

examples.text: The museum opens at 10:00 tomorrow morning.
John's plane arrives at 6:05 P.M. next Monday.

items.text: Classes ___ next week.

lines: A planned event → am / is / are + -ing: I'm meeting him tomorrow.
A timetable → simple present: The plane arrives at 6:05.

examples.text: Sam is leaving at noon tomorrow.
The museum opens at 10:00 tomorrow morning.

items.text: I'm having dinner at the airport later tonight.
I'm meeting a friend there.
We're taking a flight at midnight.
My wife has an appointment. She ___ Dr. North next Tuesday.
The museum ___ at 10:00 tomorrow morning.
John's plane ___ at 6:05 P.M. next Monday.
Look at those dark clouds. It ___ tomorrow.
items.why: Rain is not a plan. No -ing for the future.

items.text: What are you going to do this afternoon? — After lunch, I ___ a friend of mine.
Students usually TAKE four courses each semester.
Why ARE you only TAKING three?
Next semester, I AM TAKING five courses to make up.
What ARE you DOING?
I'M SENDING an email to my parents. It's their anniversary.
That's how they CELEBRATE every year.
What? Our train LEAVES in five minutes?
Yes, it LEAVES every hour on the hour.
My brother's birthday is next week. I'M GIVING him a sweater.
That's what I usually GIVE my brother.
How about a cup of coffee? — I can't. I ___ Jennifer at the library at 5:00.
items.why: A plan with a time → am meeting.

items.text: Why are you in such a hurry? — I ___ the four o'clock plane to New York.
I began smoking again. But I ___ tomorrow, and this time I mean it.
Your cough sounds terrible! — I ___ Dr. Na later this afternoon.
We're not going to fly to Canada. We ___ so we can enjoy the scenery.
This coming Saturday, I ___ my vacation of a lifetime.
My plane ___ at six-thirty Saturday morning.
I ___ at the Nusa Dua Beach Hotel.
items.why: A plan (hotel is booked) → am staying.

items.text: My plane leaves at six-thirty. Why simple present?
options: It happens every day of my life.

talk.title: My dream vacation
talk.task: Your ideal vacation starts next week! Tell Claude your plans with present forms.
talk.claudePrompt: You are my English speaking partner. Imagine I am going on my ideal vacation next week. Ask me about my plans one question at a time (When are you leaving? What time does your plane leave? Where are you staying? What are you doing on the first day?). I answer with the present progressive for my plans and the simple present for timetables. Check those two forms.

items.title: In the middle of it, later
lines: will be + verb-ing.
The activity will be in progress at a future time.

examples.text: I will be studying when you come.

items.title: Same picture, three times
lines: Yesterday, now, tomorrow at this time.
chips: Yesterday: I was sitting in class.
Now: I am sitting in class.
Tomorrow: I will be sitting in class.

items.text: Tomorrow at this time, I ___ in class.

items.title: With be going to
lines: am / is / are going to + be + -ing.
chips: I am going to be studying.
She is going to be working.

examples.text: Don't call me at nine. I am going to be studying at the library.

items.title: It also sounds softer
lines: will be + -ing can just sound more polite.
chips: I'll be picking Susie up early. (softer)

examples.text: We'll be contacting you shortly about your inquiry.

items.text: When I arrive at the airport, my whole family ___ for me.
items.why: In progress at that moment → will be waiting.

lines: will be + -ing: in progress at a time in the future.
It can also sound softer and more polite.

examples.text: I will be studying when you come.
I'll be picking Susie up early.

items.text: Right now I ___ in class.
Yesterday at this time, I ___ in class.
items.why: Yesterday at this time → was sitting.

items.text: Tomorrow at this time, I ___ in class.
items.why: Tomorrow at this time → will be sitting.

items.text: I will begin to study at seven. You will come at eight. I ___ when you come.
items.why: Already in progress at eight → will be studying.

items.text: Don't call me at nine because I won't be home. I ___ at the library.
“We'll be contacting you shortly.” How does it sound?
items.why: will be + -ing can soften the message.

items.text: Please don't call after 9:00 tonight. My husband ___ for a test.
items.why: In progress after 9:00 → will be studying.

items.text: And I ___ a project for work.
items.why: In progress at that time → will be finishing.

items.text: From early in the morning until lunch, Dr. Roberts ___ patients at her clinic.
items.why: In progress all morning → will be seeing.

items.text: After lunch, she ___ research at the hospital.
items.why: In progress then → will be doing.

items.text: In the evening, she ___ to medical students about rural health care.
items.why: In progress then → will be talking.

items.text: Jill has some medical tests tomorrow and ___ school.
items.ctx: A parent's email to a teacher

items.text: I ___ my other children at 3:00 and can get the assignments then.
Why does the parent write “I'll be picking up”, not “I'll pick up”?
options: It sounds softer and more polite.

items.text: When I ___ at the airport, my whole family will be waiting for me.
When I arrive at the airport, my whole family ___ for me.
items.why: In progress at that moment → will be waiting.

items.text: When I ___ up tomorrow morning, the sun will be shining.
When I get up tomorrow morning, the sun ___.
The birds ___.
items.why: In progress then → will be singing.
items.ctx: When I get up tomorrow morning…

items.text: And my roommate ___ in bed fast asleep.
items.why: still goes after will. lie → lying.

items.text: Just think! Two days from now I ___ in the mountains in Austria.
items.why: In progress at that time → will be skiing.

items.text: Sounds great! I ___ about you.
Are you going to be in town next Saturday? — No. I ___ my aunt in Chicago.
items.why: In progress then → will be visiting.

items.text: Where are you going to be this evening? — I ___ on my research paper at the library.
items.why: In progress this evening → will be working.

items.text: “Hey Prof! How's it going? I need an extension. Thanx ☺”
“Dear Professor Wilson, I'm sorry, but I won't be in class tomorrow. My mother is having surgery…”
items.why: A greeting, a reason, full sentences.

items.text: “Hope ur doing OK. Sorry i missed ur class. Please send one ASAP!!!”
Which opening is better for a professor?
Which subject line is better?
items.why: A subject line must be specific.

items.text: Which sentence sounds more polite?
options: I'll be taking my mother to the hospital.
I take my mother to hospital, OK?

items.text: Which ending is better?

talk.title: What will you be doing?
talk.task: Claude asks about exact times in your future. Answer with “I'll be …-ing”.
talk.claudePrompt: You are my English speaking partner. I am practicing the future progressive. Ask me one question at a time about exact future times: What will you be doing at 8:00 tonight? At this time tomorrow? Next Saturday afternoon? One year from now? I answer with 'I'll be + verb-ing'. Check that I use will be + -ing.

talk.title: Write to your teacher
talk.task: Write a short, polite email to a teacher: you will be absent for three days.
talk.claudePrompt: You are my English writing partner. I will write a short formal email to a teacher explaining why I will be absent for three days (the reason can be invented). Check that it has a specific subject line, 'Dear Professor/Mr./Ms. ...', full sentences, no texting language, a polite ending with my full name, and at least one future form such as 'I won't be in class' or 'I'll be ...-ing'. Tell me what is good and fix mistakes one at a time.

levels.title: Done by then
levels.full: Future Perfect and Future Perfect Progressive

items.title: Finished before a future time
lines: will have + past participle.
Look back from a point in the future.

examples.text: I will graduate in June. I will see you in July.
By the time I see you, I will have graduated.

items.title: by the time + present
lines: by the time + simple present, … will have + part 3.
chips: by the time I see you

items.text: By the time Violet retires, she ___ as a nurse for 40 years.

items.title: How long by then?
lines: will have been + -ing shows how long.

examples.text: I will have been sleeping for two hours by the time Ed gets home.

items.title: Often both are OK
lines: With for + time, both forms can mean the same.
chips: he will have taught for 45 years
he will have been teaching for 45 years
items.tip: These two tenses are rare. Just know them when you see them.

items.text: When Roger leaves the hospital next week, he ___ there for a week.
items.why: Looking back from that future moment → will have stayed.

lines: will have + past participle: finished before a future time.
will have been + -ing: how long, by a future time.

examples.text: By the time I see you, I will have graduated.
I will have been sleeping for two hours by the time Ed gets home.

items.text: Leo will work until December 30th, and then he will retire.
items.why: First he works, then he retires.

items.text: When Leo retires, he will have worked at the same company for 30 years.
items.why: will have worked = before he retires.

items.text: I will graduate in June. I will see you in July. By the time I see you, I ___.
items.why: Finished before July → will have graduated.

items.text: I will have been sleeping for two hours by the time Ed ___ home.
items.why: After by the time → simple present.

items.text: When Professor Jones retires next month, he ___ for 45 years.
items.why: Both perfect forms are OK here.

items.text: When Leo retires, he ___ at the same company for 30 years.
items.why: How long by then → will have been working.

items.text: Roger will get to the hospital early tomorrow. He ___ there for a week.
items.why: Just a future plan → will stay.

items.text: When Roger leaves the hospital, he ___ there a week.
items.why: Looking back from that moment → will have stayed.

items.text: After Roger has back surgery, he ___ to the recovery room.
When Roger wakes up, he ___ asleep for six hours.
items.why: How long before he wakes → will have been.

items.text: When Roger first walks, he ___ assistance.
By the time Roger can walk unassisted, he ___ many hours of physical therapy.
items.why: Before that time → will have had.

items.text: Several specialists ___ Roger by the time he goes home.
items.why: by the time … → will have helped.

missions.title: Ann and Andy, and the airport

items.text: Today is June 15th. They ___ married for two weeks.
items.ctx: Ann and Andy got married on June 1st.

items.text: By June 8th, they ___ married for one week.
items.why: Before a past date → had been.
items.ctx: Today is June 15th. Married on June 1st.

items.text: By June 29th, they ___ married for four weeks.
items.why: Before a future date → will have been.
items.ctx: Today is June 15th. Married on June 1st.

items.text: This traffic is terrible. By the time we ___ to the airport, Yuri's plane will have arrived.
items.why: After by the time (future) → simple present.

items.text: By the time we get to the airport, Yuri's plane ___.
items.why: Before we get there (future) → will have arrived.

items.text: The traffic was terrible. By the time we ___ to the airport, Yuri's plane had arrived.
items.why: A past story → simple past: got.

items.text: By the time we got to the airport, Yuri's plane ___.
items.why: Before a past moment → had already arrived.

items.text: I came to class at 9:00. Right now it is 10:00. I ___ at this desk for an hour.
items.why: Up to now → have been sitting.

items.text: By 9:30, I ___ here for half an hour.
items.why: Before a past time → had been sitting.
items.ctx: I came at 9:00. Now it is 10:00.

items.text: By 11:00, I ___ here for two hours.
items.why: Before a future time → will have been sitting.
items.ctx: I came at 9:00. Now it is 10:00.

items.text: The school bus is late. When the bus gets to school, classes ___.
items.why: Before the bus arrives → will have begun.

items.text: The teachers ___ since 9:00.
items.why: How long by then → will have been teaching.
items.ctx: When the late bus gets to school…

items.text: I'm checking flights right now. By the time you come back from lunch, I ___ our reservation.
items.why: A finished result → will have made.

items.text: This is a long car ride. By the time we arrive in Phoenix, we ___ for 20 hours straight.
items.why: How long, non-stop → will have been driving.

items.text: Don't worry about this work. By the time you get back, we ___ the project.
items.why: finish = one completed act → will have finished.

items.text: By the time the swimmers reach the finish line, they ___ steadily for more than two hours.
items.why: How long, without stopping → will have been swimming.

talk.title: By 2035, I will have…
talk.task: Tell Claude 4 things you will have done by 2035.
talk.claudePrompt: You are my English speaking partner. I am practicing the future perfect. Ask me one question at a time: What will you have done by the end of this year? By 2030? By 2035? By the time you are 50? I answer with 'I will have + past participle'. Check the form will have + past participle and that I use the simple present after 'by the time'.

items.text: Marnie will [makes] a good project manager. She has strong leadership skills.
options: Marnie will to make a good project manager. She has strong leadership skills.
Marnie will make a good project manager. She has strong leadership skills.
Marnie wills make a good project manager. She has strong leadership skills.

items.text: Where [you will] be after the game finishes?
options: Where will you be after the game finishes?
Where you will be after the game will finish?
Where will you be after the game will finish?
items.why: Question: will + subject. After after → present.

items.text: The car [no will] start. Maybe it has a dead battery.
options: The car will no start. Maybe it has a dead battery.
The car isn't start. Maybe it has a dead battery.
The car won't start. Maybe it has a dead battery.

items.text: I [going] to look for a new apartment when my roommate [move] out.
options: I am going to look for a new apartment when my roommate moves out.
I am going to look for a new apartment when my roommate will move out.
I going to look for a new apartment when my roommate moves out.
items.why: am going to. After when → moves.

items.text: After the movie [end], we are going to go out for ice cream.
options: After the movie will end, we are going to go out for ice cream.
After the movie ends, we are going to go out for ice cream.
After the movie is going to end, we are going to go out for ice cream.

items.text: By the time I am 60, my daughter will [has finish] medical school.
options: By the time I am 60, my daughter will has finished medical school.
By the time I am 60, my daughter will have finish medical school.
By the time I am 60, my daughter will have finished medical school.

items.text: Don't worry, honey. Your dad will [picking] you up soon.
options: Don't worry, honey. Your dad will be picking you up soon.
Don't worry, honey. Your dad will picks you up soon.
Don't worry, honey. Your dad will to pick you up soon.

items.text: My appointment is for 10:15 tomorrow. What time will we be [leave] here?
options: My appointment is for 10:15 tomorrow. What time will we be left here?
My appointment is for 10:15 tomorrow. What time will we be leaving here?
My appointment is for 10:15 tomorrow. What time will we be leaves here?

items.text: As soon as the term [will be] over, I [apply] for a part-time job.
options: As soon as the term will be over, I will apply for a part-time job.
As soon as the term is over, I apply for a part-time job.
As soon as the term is over, I am going to apply for a part-time job.
items.why: as soon as + present. Main part: future.

items.text: By their next anniversary, my parents will [have together] for 43 years.
options: By their next anniversary, my parents will have been together for 43 years.
By their next anniversary, my parents will be together for 43 years.
By their next anniversary, my parents will has been together for 43 years.
